resources.title: Introduction to Arts: History; Origin and Types.
resources.description: Theme: ARTS | Sub-theme: ARTS | Content: 1. Definition of Arts. 2. History and Origin of Arts: i). Early man ii) Nigerian Arts 3. Categories/Types of Art: i). Textile design. ii). Ceramics design iii) Graphics design iv). Aesthetics (Beautification and Decoration)
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define Arts. 2. trace the History and Origin of Arts, 3. identify the types of Arts.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses the definition of Art. 2. Explains the History/Origin of Art 3. Discusses the Types of Arts.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion of the definition of Art. 2. Listen to the explanations of the History/Origin of Art. 3. Participate in the discussions of types of Arts.
resources.resources: Illustrations, Printed Materials, Book Covers, Sample of Art works, Slides, Charts, Calendar, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define Art. 2. explain History and Origin of Art. 3. mention the types of Art in the Society.

resources.title: Types of Crafts.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of Crafts. 2. Types of Crafts: i. Fabric Craft like woven cloth, tie and dye ii. Paper mache iii. Carving Craft like sculpture. iv. Woven Craft like iron window, iron gate, etc. 3. Examples of types of Crafts:  Fabric tie and dye  Paper – Kite, Paper Mache.  Moulded Craft – Vases.  Carving – wood, Calabash  Woven – basketry 4. Uses of Crafts:  Beautification  culture
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of Crafts. 2. list types of Crafts. 3. Give examples of the types of Crafts. 4. state the uses of Crafts.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of Crafts. 2 . Explains the uses of Crafts. 3. Displays different Craft items.

Students: Listen and observe the display of different craft items.
resources.resources: Tie and Dye Fabric, Flower vases, Moulded Lizard, Clay products, Carved wood, Calabash.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of Craft. 2. mention 2 types of Crafts giving two examples of each.

resources.title: Practical works In Tie and Dye Using Different Methods.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of Tie and Dye. 2. Methods of tying: i). Tying ii). Clamping iii). Folding 3. Materials and Tools for tie and dye: i). Fabric ii). Dye pigment iii). Chemical (Caustic Soda, Hydrochloride) iv). Plastic bowls v). Gloves. vi) Wooden sticks 4. Preparation of dye bath. 5. Dying process.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. prepare the Dye solution. 2. design and dye Fabric in one colour using : i). Tying method ii). Clamping method iii). Folding method. 3. list materials and tools used for tie and dye.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning and types of Tie and Dye. 2. Explains and shows students the different materials and tools used in Tie and Dye. 3. Shows how to prepare the Dye bath 4. Demonstrates how to tie, fold and Clamp Fabrics. 5. Demonstrates how to dye designed fabric. 6. Displays Dyed Fabrics

Students: 1. Listen to explanation of the meaning of Tie and Dye. 2. Observe and carry out the following: i). Tying of fabrics using the different tying methods ii) follow teacher’s example in preparing the dye bath iii). dye designed fabric and display the fabric iv). dispose of used and spent dye solution appropriately.
resources.resources: Samples of tied and dyed of fabric, dye stuff, plain unstarched cotton fabric, raffia, plastic bowl, gloves, cloth line, pegs.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of tie and dye. 2. identify three types of fabric decoration. 3. name six materials for tie and dye and explain their uses. 4. make three designs on pieces of fabric. 5. prepare dye bath. 6. dye designed fabric. 7. display finished products.

resources.title: Paper Craft using Folding Technique.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of Paper Craft, 2. Materials and tools for making paper craft. 3. Methods of folding in paper craft making:  Square  Triangular folding  Rectangular  Pleating 4. Paper Craft production e.g. Kite, Greeting Card, Hand Fan.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of Paper Craft. 2. identify the materials and tools for Folding Technique. 3. list the methods of folding used in paper craft. 4. produce a paper craft e.g. Kite, Greeting Card, Hand Fan.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of Paper Craft. 2. Displays materials used in Paper Craft production. 3. Demonstrates method used in making Paper Craft namely pleating rectangular and triangular folds.

Students: Listen and watch demonstrations of methods used in making paper craft.
resources.resources: Paper, Threads, Crepe Paper, Markers, Colours, Gum, Scissors, Ruler, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify materials and tools for paper folding. 2. list method of folding in paper craft. 3. use any of the methods to produce a named Paper Craft.

resources.title: Collage Production
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of Collage. 2. Materials for Collage making e.g. Coloured Magazines, Scissors, Paper Gum, Cardboard, Drawing book, Pencil. 3. Method of producing Collage.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of Collage making. 2. identify materials for Collage. 3. describe the method of making Collage.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of Collage. 2. Mentions materials for Collage 3. Demonstrates method of producing Collage.

Students: 1. Listen to the explanation of Collage. 2. Identify materials for Collage making. 3. Make collages
resources.resources: . Coloured Magazines, Scissors, Paper Gum, Cardboard, Drawing books, Pencils
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of Collage 2. list materials for making Collage. 3. produce a Collage work.

resources.title: Modelling with Paper Mache’.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of paper Mache/ Clay. 2. Materials made from clay and paper Mache’ e.g. household utensils such as Plates, Cups, Decorations, Vases, Wall hangings, Moulded animals, etc. 3. Processes of modelling using clay/paper Mache’ :  Paper Mache’ preparation.  Using Paper Mache’ to mould an object.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. list products made from Mashed paper. 2. explain the methods of making models with mashed paper.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Shows samples of finished products. 2. Explains the methods of making models using paper mache’. 3. Demonstrates how to prepare paper mache’. 4. Asks Students to mould objects using paper mache’.

Students: 1. Actively participate in discussion of modelling with paper mache’. 2. Participate in modelling using paper mache’.
resources.resources: Old Newspaper, Paper gum, Spatula, Wooden Boards, Finished paper mache’ works, Hard boards, photographs.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention 4 house hold products that can be made from paper mache’. 2. discuss the process of preparing paper mache’. 3. mould 2 objects using paper mache’.

resources.title: Bead Work
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Definition of Bead work. 2. Production of Beads jewellery using:  beads  Roll paper  Seeds  Straw  Small pieces of wood.  Bottle tops, etc. 3. Uses of Beaded jewelleries.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what Beads are. 2. produce Beaded jewellery 3. state uses of Beads.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of Bead works. 2. Guides Students in cutting, rolling, gumming and stringing of Beads. 3. Assists Students to prepare straw, seeds and other materials for Bead work. 4. Makes jewellery with paper, seeds, beads straw etc. 5. States Uses of Beads.

Students: 1. Explain the art of Bead making. 2. Participate in the production of Beaded works like necklace, bangles, ear rings, etc. 3. Mention uses of beads.
resources.resources: Roll paper, straw, seeds, bottle tops, elastic thread, threads, needles, scissors, jewellery, small pieces of woods, beads etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. name materials for bead making. 2. make a set of jewellery from beads.

resources.title: Mosaics.
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of Mosaics. 2. Materials/Tools for making Mosaics. 3. Uses of Mosaics e.g. jewellery, flower vases, greeting cards, wall hanging. 5. Making of Mosaic projects.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of Mosaics. 2. list materials /tools used in making Mosaics. 3. enumerate uses of Mosaics. 4. make a Mosaic project e.g. wall hanging
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. States meaning of Mosaics. 2. Displays materials /tools for Mosaic making. 3. Mentions uses of Mosaics. 3. Demonstrates how to make a Mosaic project, e.g. necklace.

Students: 1. Listen attentively and ask questions. 2. Examine materials /tools used in Mosaic making. 4. Discuss uses of Mosaics.
resources.resources: Broken bottles, broken China ware, bottle tops, beads, sequins, pen, cartridge, paper plier, knives, paint, brushes, scissors, old newspaper, glue, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of Mosaics. 2. name 6 materials/ tools used in making Mosaics. 3. mention 3 uses of Mosaic. 4. make a named Mosaic article e.g. wall paper, wall hanging, etc.

resources.title: Theory of music: a). Fundamentals of Music)
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: 1. Definition: Theory of music: the study of music in its entirety, how music works, the language and notation, and elements of music. 2. Fundamentals of music:  Pitch  Melody  Harmony  Rhythm  Texture  Timbre  Quality  Form or structure 3. Notes on the Key Board.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define the theory of music 2. define the fundamentals of music. 2. state the fundamentals of music. 3. identify notes on the key board,
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines the theory of music 2. Outlines and explains the fundamentals of music. 3. Leads the class in discussion on fundamentals of music. 4. Guides the students to represent the appropriate notation in their manuscripts e.g pitch, rhythm, texture etc. 5. Guides the students to identify notes on the keyboard.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and copy notes. 2. Use their manuscripts to write notes. 3. Draw the different lines, spaces and name them. 4. Sing or play the scale
resources.resources: Music manuscripts, Pianos, Recorders, Chalkboard/magic boards, textbooks, note books.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define and state the theory of music 2. list the fundamentals of music. 3. mention two they have drawn in the music manuscripts.

resources.title: b). Ear training and Harmony
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: 1. Ear training which is aural skills or the ability to recognize music other than notation 2. Rudiments of harmony in two part writing and four part writing
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain ear training. 2. explain 4- part harmony. 2. state the rudiments of harmony. 4. explain 2 -part harmony.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lists and explains the components of harmony.

Students: 1. Listen and note down teacher’s explanation 2. Participate in a two or four part singing.
resources.resources: Music manuscript, Chalkboard/magi c boards, Pianos, Recorders, Textbooks, note books.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. play a tune with the recorder on a given scale. 2. name the components of harmony.

resources.title: Rudiments of Music
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: 1. Musical alphabets. 2. Clef and names of the staves 3. Types of staff; - treble - Bass - Great stave 4. Musical notes and their relative value. 5. Major scale of C natural. - Definition - application.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the musical alphabets 2. draw and name the staves, lines and spaces 3. identify different types of staff/ stave using clef signs 4. recognize and name the notes in the modern usage 5. identify the relative values of the notes. 6. define a scale.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides Students to recognize the types of staff /stave. 2. Guides the students to draw line and spaces, bass, treble and the great stave. 3. Explains the relationship in value between one note and the next 4. Construct a series of notes from C in alphabetical order up to it’s eighth degree (octave). 5. Assists the Students to identify the notes on a key board instrument.

Students: 1. Name the musical alphabets and types of stave. 2. Draw the different lines and name the lines and spaces. 3. Identify each musical note by: (1) describing the shape (2) reproducing the notes and their values. 4. Sing the scale produced using solfa names. 5. Sing a melody using solfa notation.
resources.resources: Music manuscripts, flash cards, pianos, descent recorders , modulators.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. name the seven musical alphabets 2. draw the great stave. 3. give the letter names of the treble stave. 4. list the six musical notes in the descending order of their valves. 5. draw the diatonic scale of a major key (C or G).

resources.title: Playing an instrument (Recorder)
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: 1. The Recorder: This is an instrurment in the woodwind family that come in soprano, alto and tenor versions. 2. Uses of a recorder: Good for music beginers, useful for sight reading and developing listening skills. 3. Key Signatures of a recorder. 4. Steps of playing the recorder
resources.objectives: Students should be Able to: 1. explain what a recorder is. 2. state the uses of a recorder 3. name the key signatures of a recorder 4. explain how to play the recorder
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the nature and uses of the Recorder while playing for emphasis. 2. Writes the key signatures for the students to copy in their music manuscripts. 3. Enumerates steps in playing the recorder.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanation and take notes. 2. Listen to teacher’s explanation on basic steps to play the recorder. 3. Play a tune with the recorder.
resources.resources: Recorders, Music manuscripts, Chalkboard/ma gic boards, text books, note books.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. identify an alto, tenor or soprano recorder; 2. state three steps of playing the recorder. 3. individual performance of the recorder.

resources.title: Use of music
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: 1. Uses of music - for ritual purpose & - for ceremonial purpose - Advertisement - Healing - Work - Communication - Education - Sport 2. Impact of music in the society. i). During important occasions. ii). At Joyous moments. iii). Creating employment.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to : 1 States the uses of music in the society. 2. State the impact of music on human life
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Illustrate uses of music in festivals,  worship,  advertisement  Healing etc. 2, Guides students in enumerating the impact of music in society .

Students: 1. Students participate in discussing the uses of music 2. Describe ways in which music can affect human lives.
resources.resources: Radio, Tape recorders pictures showing performing musicians.
resources.assessment: Students to; 1. State three uses of music in the locality 2. State four ways music can have impact on their lives and the society.

resources.title: Definition of Drama and Theatre
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Definition of Drama: A Type of literature usually written to be performed. Also an imitation of an action, e.g. Trials of Brother Jero and The Lion and the Jewel by Wole Soyinka etc. 2. Theatre is the performance as well as the Place where a performance takes place. 3. People involved in drama/theatre like: Playwright Director Actor Designers Audience etc
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define Drama 2. define theatre 3 .list people involved in drama and theatre
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1 Defines drama with examples from local environment e.g. Masquerade performance. 2. Lists and explains the duties of the people in the theatre.

Students: 1. Listen and copy notes. 2. In groups, play the role of actor / actress and audience in turns.
resources.resources: Chalkboard/magic board, script, textbook showing pictorials of theatre .
resources.assessment: Students to 1. state the meaning of drama and the meaning of theatre. 2. list 5 people involved in a drama/theatre.

resources.title: Functions of Drama
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Functions of drama: 1. Education (Teaching values among other things) 2. Information 3. Entertainment 4. Therapeutic 5. Development
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state functions of drama
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lists and explains functions of drama.

Students: 1. Listen and take down notes on the explanation of functions. 3. Watch a video recorded drama on any of these: examination malpractice, greed, idleness etc.
resources.resources: Chalkboard/magic board., Video / audio recorded drama, Live drama
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list five functions of drama. 2. mention one way in which a given drama portrays any of the functions.

resources.title: Elements of Drama.
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Elements of Drama: i) Script/improvisation (plot, diction, ii) Characters iii) Stage (setting, iv) Audience v) Sound (songs, music,, sound effect) vi) Lights, etc. 2. Identifying elements in drawn.3. Creating elements in drama.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. name the elements of drama 2. identify the elements in a given drama. 3. create any of the elements.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes and explains the different elements of drama on chalkboard. 2. Shows the video recording of a drama. 4. Guides students to identify the elements in the drama shown. 5. Calls on students to demonstrate some of the elements of drama.

Students: 1 Listen to the explanations of different elements of drama and take down notes. 2. Watch video recorded drama. 3. Identify the elements of drama in the drama shown. 5. Demonstrate or explain some of the elements.
resources.resources: Chalkboard/magic boards, Video/audio recorded drama, textbooks, notebooks.
resources.assessment: Students to : 1. list three elements of drama. 2. identify three elements of drama in the recommended drama shown.. 3. create any two elements of drama.

resources.title: Forms of Drama
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Forms of drama: Comedy and Tragedy.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify the category of a given drama. 2. mention the forms of drama.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lists and explains the two forms of Drama

Students: 1. Listen and copy notes on the two forms of drama.
resources.resources: Chalk board/magic board, text book, notebooks.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list two basic forms of drama.

resources.title: Origin of Drama.
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Origin of Drama: Drama is said to have originated from three sources: Mimesis, Ritual and Storytelling. 2. Dramatic elements of Festivals, Storytelling: Dialogue, Action Audience, Stage etc
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the origin of drama 2. identify the type of drama they have watched on stage or on Video.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lists and explains the origin of drama. 2. Encourages pupils to narrate some form of drama they have experienced in their immediate environment.

Students: 1. Listen and copy notes. 2. Narrate some dramatic experiences they have observed around them.
resources.resources: Chalk board/magic board, Textbook, note books, pictorials or illustrations of ritual/festival, storyteller, Ancient man hunting game.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. give three sources where drama originated from; 2. write an essay about a festival or story telling session they have watched on television, bringing out the dramatic elements.

resources.title: Playwriting
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Playwriting 2. Categories of dramatists/playwrights. * Classical (Universal) * Modern * Contemporary 3. The duties of a playwright:: Conceives the idea of the play Develop the story through the plot Develop the characters through their dialogues and actions 4. Infuse in locale and situations Pays attention to the stage directions, transitions, high point etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to 1. State what playwriting is; 2. state who a playwright is; 3. mention the duties of a playwright. 4. name some popular playwrights in Nigeria and outside Nigeria. 5. mention the categories of playwrights
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what playwriting is. 2. Explains who a dramatist playwright is. 3. Lists the categories of playwrights on chalkboard. 4. Mentions and explains the work of a Playwright. 5. Explains the three categories of dramatist/playwrig hts given examples.

Students: 1. Listen to the explanation of the teacher and take notes.
resources.resources: Chalk board, Flash cards containing names and categories of playwrights, text book, note books, Copies of plays.
resources.assessment: Students to : 1. state what playwriting is; 4. state who a playwright is 2. list the three categories of playwrights. 3. give names of two classical dramatists/playwright 4. mention three modern playwrights. 5. give the names of three playwrights in Nigeria

resources.title: The Director.
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. The play Director: lists duties of the play directors 2. He is the boss of the theatre. 3. He coordinates all the other aspects of production 4. He casts and rehearses the actors by blocking and guiding their movements 5. He interprets the scripts and puts a live drama on stage etc. 6. He coordinates the work and art of every other person and makes everything blend for the production. 7. He is responsible for the production seen on stage.etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state who a director is. 2. mention the duties of a director. 3. mention the functions of the director in the theatre.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains who a director is and his/her duties. 2. Guides students with leadership abilities to try to direct a given play.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s explanation and copy down notes. 2. Participate in the try- outs guided by the teacher.
resources.resources: Chalk board, Flash cards, Drama scripts, text book, note books.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state who a director is. 2. give three functions of the director. 3. List four duties of the director.

resources.title: Costume and Make-up in Drama.
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Meaning of costume: Clothing and accessories (caps, shoes, jewelleries) worn by a performer on stage. 2. What is Make-up? Application of all forms of powder and paint on the performer. 3. Types of make-up: Straight make-up. Character make-up. 4. Uses of Make-up:  Alter appearance  Enhance appearance. 5. Make-up items:  Powder  Lipstick  Wig  Eye pencil  Native Chalk  Camwood etc
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what is meant by costume. 2. explain what make-up is. 3. state the two basic types of make-up. 4. state the uses of make-up and costume in Drama. 5. mention some costume and make-up items.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains costume and writes the explanation on Chalkboard. 2. Explains make- up and writes the explanation on chalkboard. 3. Mentions the two basic types of make-up. 4. Mentions and explains the uses of costume and make-up 4. Displays example of costumes and make-up items for students. 5.Leads students to work on costume and make-up for their play production

Students: 1. Listen and copy notes on teacher’s explanation of costume and make-up. 2. Observe displayed costume and make-up. 3. . Participate in creating a costume and make-up chart for the class play production.
resources.resources: . Chalk board/magic board ,F lash cards, text books, note books, Make- up items e.g eye pencils, powder, lip sticks. Pictorials of costume and make-up.
resources.assessment: Students to : 1. state meaning of costume. 2. state the meaning of make-up. 3. mention the two basic types of make-up. 4. Mention 2 uses of costume and make-up. 5. List five make- up items.

resources.title: Definition of Dance
resources.description: Theme: DANCE | Sub-theme: DANCE | Content: 1. Meaning of dance: Movement of the body in space and time to express an idea or pass across a message. 2. Uses of dance: Dance entertains Passes important information and messages like Unity, love, tolerance etc. enliven the mood of an occasion. etc. 3. How to dance.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define dance; 2. state the uses of dance. 3. perform some dance movements
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines dance. 2. Explains the components of movement, space, time, expression. 3. Enumerates the uses of dance with examples. 4. Leads the class in a discussion on the uses of dance they have observed in their immediate environment. 5. Leads the students in performing some dance movements

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s explanation and take notes 2. Participate in the discussion on the uses of dance. 3. Participate in the practical dance class
resources.resources: Textbook, note books, chalkboard/magic board, pictorials of various dances, CD or cassette player or drums, gong and rattle, proper clothing for dance (Tights, Leotard, T shirt)
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of dance 2. describe four uses of dance and give one example each. 3. display two dance movements/phras es that express a particular idea or emotion.

resources.title: Introduction to Choreography.
resources.description: Theme: DANCE | Sub-theme: DANCE | Content: 1. Meaning of Choreography: The art of making and arrangement of dances. 2. Principles of choreography:  order  beauty,  variety etc, 3. Meaning of Choreographer: A theatre artist who creates, arranges dances, teaches dancers to perform a dance to the delight of an audience.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define choreograph y 2. state some principles of choreograph y 3. explain the term ‘choreograph er’.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the terms ‘ choreography’ and ‘choreographer’ 2. Explains some principles of choreography. 3. Leads the class in performing a choreographed dance using music or any other tool.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s explanation and take down notes. 2. Participate in class dance and choreography session.
resources.resources: Textbook, notebooks, Chalk board, magic board, CD player, musical instruments, dance outfits.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of choreography. 2. describe who a choreographer is. 3. state two things a choreographer does that is different from a dancer.

resources.title: Contemporary Dance.
resources.description: Theme: DANCE | Sub-theme: DANCE | Content: 1. Meaning of contemporary dance: A form of dance that is a clear departure from the traditional and ballet dance forms but draws inspiration from them. 2. Features of Contemporary dance:  Individual style  Creativity  Does not have fixed movements etc. 3. Performing some contemporary dance movements.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of contemporary dance. 2. discuss some features of contemporary dance. 3. Mention some contemporary dance movements. 4. Perform some contemporary dance movement.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines and explains contemporary dance. 2. Plays video of contemporary dance; Nigerian and Western. 3. Leads the class in a discussion of points they have noted. 4. Introduces various contemporary dance movements. 5. Guides the student(s) to perform some movements to build and encourage individual creativity.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanation 2. Watch video of contemporary dance. 3. Participate in class discussion of what they have noticed. 4. Perform some dance movements portraying their understanding of contemporary dance..
resources.resources: Textbook, notebooks, chalk board/magic boards, DVDs/VCDs players, television, sets.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of contemporary dance 2. explain two specific things they noticed while watching the video. 3. display two dance movements they have been learning and practicing. 4. exhibit a solo or a group dance

resources.title: Team Work and Sense of Belonging
resources.description: Theme: WORK ETHICS | Sub-theme: WORK ETHICS | Content: 1. Meaning of Team Work. 2. Importance of Team Work. 3. Meaning of Sense of Belonging. 4. How to achieve Sense of Belonging.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of team work. 2. state the importance of team work. 3. explain the meaning of sense of belonging. 4. state how to achieve sense of belonging in the society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the following: i). Meaning of team work ii). Importance of team work. iii). Sense of Belonging. iv) How to achieve Sense of belonging. 2. Leads group of students to dramatize how to achieve team work and sense of belonging.

Students: 1. State the meaning of team work and sense of belonging. 2. Explain the importance of Team work. 3. Demonstrate how to achieve Team work and Sense of belonging.
resources.resources: Charts showing: - Members of a community, - Young people working as a group . People of different tribes hugging themselves.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the importance of Team work 2. mention three benefits of team work.

resources.title: Consequences of Using Fake and Adulterated Goods.
resources.description: Theme: WORK ETHICS | Sub-theme: WORK ETHICS | Content: 1, Meaning of Fake and Adulterated Goods. 2. Goods often faked and adulterated:  Medicine  Processed foods  Clothing  Fabrics, etc. 3. Reasons why people produce and distribute fake and adulterated goods:  Greed  Lack of patriotism.  Lack of morals  Disloyalty. 4. How to stop the sale of fake and adulterated goods:  Be patriotic  Show love for your people.  Be honest  Respect authority  Know your right as a consumer. 5. Teacher: 1. Explains meaning of Crocheting. 2. Displays materials/tools used in Crocheting. 3. Demonstrates how to make basic Crocheting stitches.

Students: 1. Listen attentively. 2. Observe as teacher demonstrates with the materials/tools used in Crocheting. 3. Practice making crocheting stitches.
resources.resources: Crocheting pins, wools, cotton thread, specimen of finished work.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of Crocheting. 2. list 5 materials/tools used in Crocheting 3. practice Crocheting stitches. 4. Display finished work.

resources.title: Batik Work
resources.description: Theme: CRAFTS | Sub-theme: CRAFTS | Content: 1. Meaning of Batik. 2. Materials /tools used in Batik work. 3. Making Batik project: i). Technique ii). Processes
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of Batik. 2. list materials /tools for Batik work. 3. make Batik project.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains how to do Batik work. 2. Displays materials /tools for Batik work. 3. Prepares fabrics for batik work. 4. Demonstrates how to make batik work.

Students: 1. Observe and touch materials /tools for Batik work. 2. Prepare fabrics with wax. 3. Dye fabric after wax application.
resources.resources: Fabrics, wax, old newspaper, dye stuff, printing table, oye bath stove, gas cooker, pot for melting wax.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the meaning of Batik. 2. name five materials /tools for Batik. 3. make Batik project. 4. display finished work.

resources.title: Uses of Music.
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: Uses of Music: For Ritual For ceremonies In Church Advertisement Propaganda Education Entertainment Stress relief etc 2. Impact of Music:  Helps build relationships  Helps foster brotherliness  Creates awareness in the mass media  It is the soul of life etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the uses of music in society. 2 state the impact of music on human life.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the uses of music during different occasions mentioned. 2. Leads the class to enumerate and discuss the impact of music in society.

Students: 1.Listen and copy notes. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Sing any known song together accompanying it with hand clapping or percussion.
resources.resources: Chalkboard, magic boards, text books, note books, Musical CDs, available percussion instruments.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state five uses of music; 2. state four ways music can impact society. 3. singing together.

resources.title: Creating Music/Solf a Notation values.
resources.description: Theme: MUSIC | Sub-theme: MUSIC | Content: 1. Music Values 2. Setting words to solfa 3. Rhythm
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. write values of solfa 2. formulate words to set to solfa notation 3. clap a rhythm
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explain what solfa values mean 2. Guides students to compose a song text using a poem. 3. Fixes solfa values on words. 4. Guides students to clap rhythms of song/texts. 5. Plays a phrase for students to emulate

Students: 1. Bar given solfa names. 2. Compose a text using a popular tune 3. Fix the solfa names of the text 4. Clap rhythms 5. Listen to teacher’s playing and emulates
resources.resources: Music manuscripts, Chalkboards, magic boards,
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain what a complete rehearsal is. 2. compose a text 3. Bar the phrase 4. clap rhythm.

resources.title: Drama and the development of rural communities.
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: Drama and theatre for development.: This type of drama highlights community issues and problems in order to motivate them to carry out self help programmes rather than always wait for the government to do everything for them.
resources.objectives: The Students should be able to: 1. state how drama and theatre can be used to develop rural communities. 2. setting a storyline into drama.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what theatre for development stands for. 2. Leads students in a class discussion on the state of rural communities and how drama can be used to help the people. 3. Explains ways drama can assist the rural people.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and copy notes. 2. Participate in class discussion on theatre and development. 3. 3. Explain how drama can help to solve some community problems.
resources.resources: Chalkboard/magic boards, textbooks, note books, pictorials of some community problems like bad roads, lack of pipe borne water.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1 mention two ways drama helps to solve community problems. 2. Identify four community problems. 3. mention 4 ways drama can bring solution to community problems.

resources.title: Opportunities for career dramatists
resources.description: Theme: DRAMA | Sub-theme: DRAMA | Content: 1. Career prospects for dramatists: Playwrights Directors Actors Designers. 2. How they affect society: Each of them makes significant contribution to society.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. mention the career prospects of dramatists 2. state ways dramatists affect the society
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the prospects in building a career in drama. 2. Leads the class in a discussion of how their creative works impact society 3. Give names of Notable Nigerians in each category

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s explanation and copy notes. 2. Participate in the discussion of how dramatists impact the society 3. Participate in class discussion of some dramatists they may know.
resources.resources: Textbook, note book, Pictorials, Chalkboard/magic boards.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list two career prospects of an actor and a director. 2. state two ways dramatists have impacted society 3. give names of five popular actors/actresses in Nigeria.

resources.title: Process of Choreograp hy
resources.description: Theme: DANCE | Sub-theme: DANCE | Content: Processes of Choreography: 1. Conception of the dance idea 2. Gathering of the movement 3. Putting and arranging the movements by teaching the dancers. 4. Creating the final structure and polishing it for performance.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the processes a choreographer needs to employ to create a dance. 2. creating dance pattern. .
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Mentions and explains the processes of choreography. 2. Leads students in a class discussion on Chorography. 3. Guides students to choreograph a 10 minute dance piece. 4. Explains the use of space and gestures.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and copy notes. 2. Participate in the class discussion.. 3. Participate in the class exercises.
resources.resources: Chalkboard/magic boards, Text books, note books, Musical instruments or CDs players, dance outfits.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention the processes of choreography 2. discuss in groups how they intend to apply the processes 3. create a 10 minute dance piece for presentation during a school programmes.

resources.title: Prospects of Studying dance in Nigeria
resources.description: Theme: DANCE | Sub-theme: DANCE | Content: Prospects of dance in Nigeria: 1. Dance can be a good income earner for the government and the performer. 2. It can also bring in foreign exchange when used in the tourism industry like carnivals 3. Dance as a cultural indicator and promoter.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the prospects of dance 2. discuss the prospects of dance
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. States and explains to students the lucrative nature of dance. 2. Leads the class in a discussion of the prospects of dance.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s explanation and write notes. 2. Participate in the class discussion on the prospects of dance
resources.resources: Textbooks, note books, chalkboard/magic boards.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list Four prospects of dance 2. write a 2 page essay on why they will either be dancers or choreographe rs.

resources.title: .Unity
resources.description: Theme: UNITY | Sub-theme: UNITY | Content: 1. Meaning of unity. 2. Causes of disunity in the home, school and society. 3. How to maintain unity:  Be tolerant  Be fair to all  Be sincere  Be cautious  Respect other opinion  Be accommodating  Avoid cheating  Be honest 4. Demonstration of acts of unity
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of unity. 2. mention causes of disunity at home, school and in the society. 3. describe how to maintain unity at home and society. 4. show acts that encourage unity.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of unity. 2. Explains causes of disunity in the home, school and society. 3. Guides students to suggest and discuss how to maintain unity at home, school and society. 4. Group students to write a play on how to maintain unity at home and society emphasizing religious and cultural tolerance.

Students: 1. Discuss meaning of unity. 2. Suggest some causes of disunity in the home and society. 3. Write a play on how to maintain unity at home and society. 4. Act a play written by one of the groups.
resources.resources: The Nigerian Flag, School flag, Pictures of people united at a football pitch, charts showing the President or Governors speaking to the Nation or State, charts, pictures showing united people.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain meaning of unity. 2. mention four causes of disunity among people. 3. act a play that emphasize religious and cultural tolerance..
